item.title: California treasurer urges Trump to honor SCOTUS tariff ruling
item.description: California and nine states' financial officers urged President Trump to honor the Supreme Court's ruling striking down his tariffs, citing harm to state budgets and the need for economic predictability.

item.title: Munis see small gains, 10-year UST falls below 4%
item.description: On the week, the muni market performed well, with most investor action happening in the longer half of the curve, said BofA strategists.

item.title: Brightline West cites construction progress, still no federal loan
item.description: Brightline West told investors it is pursuing a $4 billion senior loan from a banking consortium and simultaneously working toward the $6 billion federal loan.

item.title: Vermont Bond Bank brings modernized indenture to market
item.description: The Vermont Bond Bank debuts a new indenture when it sells $56 million of bonds this week. It's following a nationwide trend in bond bank structures.

item.title: February bond issuance was flat
item.description: Issuance was $40.336 billion in 632 issues, down only 1.1% year-over-year from $40.772 billion across 731 transactions.

item.title: D.C. tax revenue spikes, decouple confusion continues
item.description: Washington, D.C.'s Office of the Chief Financial Officer released a revenue report showing higher than expected tax revenues and a local economy that's struggling.

item.title: SCOTUS will consider whether cities, states can sue oil firms over climate-change damage
item.description: Eleven states and dozens of local governments have active lawsuits against fossil fuel companies.

item.title: NFMA's new chair highlights initiatives including membership survey, white papers
item.description: NFMA "serves a lot of core functions," said Angela Kukoda, its 2026 chair.

item.title: Geopolitical shock from Operation Epic Fury tests muni market resilience
item.description: Market Intelligence analyst Jeff Lipton assesses the early impacts of Operation Epic Fury on rates, spreads, shifting inflation expectations, and flows, arguing that elevated tax-exempt income, disciplined sector allocation and a quality bias can help muni investors navigate headline-driven volatility.

item.title: Munis outperform UST selloff amid U.S.-Iran war
item.description: First thing this morning, there wasn't much action as market participants waited to see what would happen, but as the day went on, munis got progressively weaker, said Kyle Gerberding, director of trading, a portfolio manager and partner at Asset Preservation Advisors.
